processing: A cultivar, not a fixed style: its leaf suits Long Jing-type flat tea, pan-fired green and Bi Luo Chun-type curled tea, and also yellow Huang Tang.
harvest_season: Very early. The Pingyang spring harvest has started in late February to early March in recent years, ahead of most of Zhejiang.
appearance_dry: Depends on the style made; most often flat Long Jing-type or curled green leaf.
appearance_liquor: Typically a clear, pale yellow-green, as with other early Zhejiang greens.
taste_profile: Reported as good in quality but somewhat lighter than teas from some other cultivars, because of its relatively large leaf.

brewing.notes: Typical for early Zhejiang green tea. Since the cup runs light, use a little more leaf rather than longer steeps.

vintage_note: Sold only as fresh, current-year spring tea, and its whole appeal is arriving first: the earliest lots reach the market before the Qingming teas of other areas. It often appears under the name of the style made from it rather than the cultivar. Drink within the year.
description:
Pingyang Tezao, roughly Pingyang extra-early, is a tea cultivar from Pingyang in southern Zhejiang. It is a medium-leaf shrub, and you are more likely to drink it than to see its name, because it often goes into other styles.

The point of the plant is its earliness. Its leaf suits flat Long Jing-type tea, pan-fired green, curled Bi Luo Chun-type tea and yellow Huang Tang, so one early flush can feed several products.

The usual note against it is that the larger leaf gives a somewhat lighter cup than some other cultivars. Add a little more leaf instead of stretching the steep.

When buying very early Long Jing-style tea, ask what cultivar it is and where it grew. The name of the cultivar tells you about the plant, not about whether the tea comes from a protected Long Jing area.
history: The cultivar originates from Dapingcun in Aojiang town, Pingyang, and was recognised as a provincial improved variety by Zhejiang's crop variety committee in 1998. Pingyang's tea promotion credits it with helping the county's industry grow. Little else about who selected it, or when, is easy to document.
